title: Graduate-school planning conversation
session_summaries: Session 1: The user wants to apply for a research-oriented MPhil in Hong Kong or Singapore and is interested in AI agents.
Session 2: The user prefers a paper-style course project with a clear research question and manageable engineering scope.
Session 3: The user becomes interested in long-context memory and wants a project that can later grow into an agent-memory system.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to apply for a research-oriented MPhil in Hong Kong or Singapore.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then your course project should look closer to a small research prototype than a generic demo.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I am especially interested in AI agents.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The project must be realistic because I only have about two weeks.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then we should narrow the scope to one core module instead of building a full agent system.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want something that matches both industry trends and future research.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A long-context memory module is a good match because agents need to preserve user goals and conversation state.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I agree. Let's do a project on long-text memory.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: We can combine recent context, session summaries, and retrieval to build a hybrid memory system.

questions.question: What long-term degree goal does the user mention?
questions.answer: A research-oriented MPhil in Hong Kong or Singapore.

questions.question: What project topic does the user finally agree on?
Why is a long-context memory module considered a good match for agents?
questions.answer: Because agents need to preserve user goals and conversation state.
